title: Experience booking flights through Trip.com
body:
O.P.
I have never used an OTA to book flights before as always prefer to go direct through the airline's website so that dealing with future issues is easier. I am now helping my daughter book flights to Japan and as she is a uni student she is much more focussed on every last $.
I am a Citibank CC customer so have access to their 5% off promotion on Trip.com. The flights I am looking at are direct flights with JAL and they are already showing on Trip.com as $50 cheaper, so with the 5% the total saving compared to JAL's website is >$100.
Given there are no connecting flights to worry about, a JAL economy ticket is meant to be all inclusive so no additional charges like seat selection or baggage to worry about and JAL flight cancellation is highly unlikely, I am wandering if I am being too paranoid about using an OTA as there is not much left she may end up having to deal with Trip.com about.
Appreciate any thoughts and feedback given the above. I have used OTAs for accom before, but not flights and not Trip.com at all. Thanks

---- replies ----
[User #520642761 postswoodyrenWhirlpool Enthusiast] I have used Trip to book multiple domestic flights in China. Also hotels and trains. They have been very reliable and easy to deal with.
Local airlines have cancelled schedule flights a few times and Trip has quickly alerted me when this has occurred.
[User #168436•17438 postsHu_LionModerator] Trip.com is the largest travel agency in the world, even bigger than Expedia and Booking.com, so it it not one of those small, not well known travel agencies. Their size also allows them certain leverage when working out deals with travel partners.
[User #6435613518 postsMugsyEnhance your calm!Whirlpool Forums Addict] Dad's been booking flights to/from/within China from Trip.com for the past 6 months. No issues.
[User #898936212 postsLeo HSuppository of all wisdomWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
Very reliable, and responsive. The only issue I've found is when Philippine Airlines had a flight change, accepting the change through trip com wasn't reflected in the booking when I viewed it on the airline's website, until I accepted it via Philippine Airlines.
Refunds are very quick if you ever need to cancel. Like one hour or semi-instantaneous.
[User #151657469 postsstang65Forum Regular] O.P.
Thanks for the feedback, that's much more positive than I was expecting. Definitely tempted to give it a go I think.
[User #898936212 postsLeo HSuppository of all wisdomWhirlpool Forums Addict] Trip.com is very organised. When you want to cancel a flight it is clear what the cancellation fee is and exactly how much you will get back. Ditto with train cancellations. Also, I wanted to book Air Asia tickets, but it didn't like my credit cards so I went to trip com and booked through them and paid less than I would have direct. I also booked a tour them in China, but had to cancel because the tour company couldn't obtain the cable car tickets we needed and therefore couldn't proceed with the tour. Sent trip.com screenshots of the conversation with the tour operator and had a full refund in hours.
Overall, I'm happy with them so far.
[User #905785708 postsWaldaWhirlpool Enthusiast] Used them for flights, both international and domestic, and trains/hotels in china.
They have great English based support.
However, that being said, i have only used it to book Chinese airlines such as China Southern and China Eastern. I have not used it to book with foreign airlines, and not sure if they will be much better than any other OTA if something goes wrong, since they will need to deal with foreign airlines.
Feedback saying people have booked flights with them, such as myself and other above, honestly means very very little if they were Chinese airlines and there was no cancellations etc. Its when things go wrong and a flight gets cancelled, or you miss a connecting flight etc, its what happens then and then only that you will see what an OTA is like.
That being said, i continue to use trip.com to book things in china, and flights to and from china with Chinese airlines, but i wouldn't use them to book anything else.
[User #8158854370 postsYoung CodgerWhirlpool Forums Addict] Had not realised until watching a youtube video recently that Trip.com owned Skyscanner. They are certainly a big player and becoming larger outside China. My biggest problem with OTA's is the less than clear ways in which you add baggage seat and meal selection
[User #898936212 postsLeo HSuppository of all wisdomWhirlpool Forums Addict] Young Codger writes...
My biggest problem with OTA's is the less than clear ways in which you add baggage seat and meal selection
You can usually do this on trip.com at the time of booking. If available, do it, as with some Chinese airlines it becomes a pain if you don't do it at the time of booking.
[User #898936212 postsLeo HSuppository of all wisdomWhirlpool Forums Addict] One of the main benefits of trip.com is that at the time of booking, they are very clear about the fare conditions and what the cancellation and change fees are, baggage allowances etc. Some other OTAs are nowhere near as clear. And if you do need to change or cancel, that is exactly the fee charged.
[User #4162818363 postsPsyvoltWhirlpool Forums Addict] Ive only used Trip.com once, and that was to try book flights on an airline (small airline in Thailand called Nok Air) that at the time wasn't accepting payment from any of my cards (tried multiple times on multiple cards but kept saying payment failed). Trip.com was charging slightly less than what Nok was charging, so tried to book thru them after the above failed attempts – but after waiting 40 mins for my booking receipt, they said that flights had gone up in the interim and did i still want to purchase the tickets at the increased price (75% increase). Refused the price increase, and ended up booking the flights on Expedia for the same price that Nok was charging.
Hasn't put me off Trip.com thou, and if they had flights at a saving I'd still consider trying them but wouldn't be counting my chickens till i received the booking confirmation in my inbox (and money taken from my account).
[User #22974585 postsMike2003Whirlpool Enthusiast] Looking to book China Eastern tickets from Trip.com. I see they're based in Singapore? Do you need to use a foreign transaction fee free to avoid any currency exchange fees? or through paypal? And how does seat selection work with them? can you choose during booking?
[User #905785708 postsWaldaWhirlpool Enthusiast] Mike2003 writes...
And how does seat selection work with them? can you choose during booking?
I have never been able to select on trip, had to do it on the airlines website after booking on trip.
[User #8158854370 postsYoung CodgerWhirlpool Forums Addict] Walda writes...
I have never been able to select on trip, had to do it on the airlines website after booking on trip.
That's good to know Many other OTA's never give you the PRN so you have no ability to access the airline website to do add ons etc. It would certainly appear that some OTA'a are better than others. I've increasingly seen some OTA's offering "protected connections" even though the flights are self transfer on different PRN's. Would be interesting to see what this means in practice
[User #898936212 postsLeo HSuppository of all wisdomWhirlpool Forums Addict] Young Codger writes...
I've increasingly seen some OTA's offering "protected connections" even though the flights are self transfer on different PRN's. Would be interesting to see what this means in practice
Trip.com clearly spells out if you need to collect luggage and go through immigration, such as they did when I booked a connecting flight Nadi to Manila via Brisbane. They seem to be more organised on the details than others I've dealt with.
